Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team loved the latency profile and the KV-cache example. We’re close to getting internal signoff but the executive finance committee asked whether we can extend the pilot by two weeks while we complete a short integration test.

- Can Redwood provide a two-week runway bump for the existing PoC (same scope) and a transparent cost for that extension?
- If an extra credit / invoice-friendly option makes procurement easier, we’d consider that instead of a time extension.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our committee meets Friday.

Hi Danielle — thanks for sending this over and for the quick context.

Short answer: yes we can accommodate a two-week extension. Two possible approaches that usually work for procurement teams:

1) Time-extension (no change to per-token pricing) — two additional weeks added to the pilot term, with a pro-rated invoice for expected consumption. No change to SLAs.

2) Credit top-up — a one-off smaller invoice (credit) that buys an equivalent amount of capacity; this maps cleaner to PO workflows and keeps the pilot end-date unchanged on paper.

I’ve looped in Ben Carter (sales lead) and Marissa Cole (contracts) to propose exact numbers and invoice language. If Procurement needs a sample PO line item we can provide that same day.

Do you have a rough estimate of expected extra token usage over the two weeks (or do you prefer we model a conservative usage)?

I’ll follow up with concrete figures in the next 24 hours.

— Hannah

Suggested approach based on similar accounts:

- Offer A (Time): +2 weeks at current pilot rate, pro-rated based on their average daily consumption. No paperwork change beyond an amendment to the SOW. This is simplest for product/ops but can be annoying for procurement if they want a single dollar number up front.

- Offer B (Credit): Issue a $6,500 credit invoice that maps to expected token burn for 2 weeks under conservative usage. Revenue recognizes as prepaid; procurement likes the single-line invoice.

Pricing rationale: ClearValley has been averaging about 2.1M tokens/week during the pilot. At current unit economics that maps to ~3.9M tokens for two weeks. With pilot discounts (15%) and rounding for headroom, $6.5k is defensible and keeps the AR impact low.

Contract language: Marissa — if you can prepare a short amendment and a single-line credit invoice template I can approve the pricing and we’ll send it to Danielle.

Ben

Hi Danielle — following up with the two approved options so Procurement can pick the one that maps best to your PO workflow. Apologies for the slight delay; we wanted to confirm numbers with finance.

Option 1 — Time extension (preferred by engineering)
• Add 14 calendar days to the existing pilot term (no change to per-token rate).
• Amendment: short SOW addendum confirming new end date and unchanged scope.
• Invoice: pro-rated estimate for the two-week delta; final reconciliation after the pilot ends.

Option 2 — One-off credit (procurement-friendly)
• We’ll issue a single-line invoice for $6,500 labeled “Pilot capacity credit — ClearValley Health.”
• Credit will be applied to the pilot project and consumed as normal; pilot end date remains unchanged on paper.

Attachments: sample_PO_line_item.txt (inline below) and the proposed one-line invoice template. If Procurement prefers the credit approach, we can send the DocuSign and invoice the same day.

Sample PO text (suggested):
"Redwood Inference — Pilot capacity credit — $6,500 — SKU: RW-PILOT-CREDIT — Invoice due on receipt"

Next steps: tell me which option Procurement prefers and we’ll send the amendment/invoice + DocuSign link. If your committee would like a slightly smaller credit ($5k) in exchange for a short SLA exemption (lowered burst capacity), we can discuss, but Finance prefers the $6.5k for the conservative buffer.

Happy to jump on a 15-minute call today if that would speed things up.

Best,
